note:
The household of Edwin Gauntley Loverseed, living on private means, his wife Jemima and their three grown daughters, with two servants, at 2 Western Terrace (#341) on the 1911 return, transcribed by A. Hagues. 2 Western Terrace holds no census record at all in the record, so nothing is displaced, and none of the seven was held.

**He had the house for at least twenty-one years.** Wright's Directory prints 'Mr. Edwin G. Loverseed' at 2 Western Terrace in 1894-95 and 1898-99, and 'Loverseed Edwin Gauntley' at the same number in 1910-11, 1913-14 and 1915-16. With this return he is there from 1894 to 1916 without a break in the printed record - one of the longer tenancies the estate shows.

**The family is worth following beyond this house.** 'Mrs. Sarah Loverseed' is printed next door at 1 Western Terrace in 1894-95 and 1898-99, and 'Pelham lodge, Mr. Ar. W. Loverseed' on Pelham Crescent in 1894-95. The record also notes 10 and 12 Pelham Crescent as 'one of a pair of houses c1870-75 possibly by John Loverseed' - so the name attaches to a builder or architect as well as to these households. Nothing here establishes how any of them are related, so no links are made; but if one family is behind both the houses and the building of them, this is the thread.

Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1911 census, 2 Western Terrace, transcribed by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1894-95 and 1898-99, Western Terrace number 2; 1910-11, 1913-14 and 1915-16, same number.
